items_missed: No agenda statement at all — no roadmap, no 10-15 minute timeframe, no 'sound good?' confirmation.
Never asked 'how are you today?' — opened with 'how can I help?' and went straight to transactional mode.

Never confirmed availability for the customer's dates. Brandon opened with 'next Thursday or Friday' and later said 'the tenth or the eleventh' of September; Joel never checked the calendar or confirmed either date was open.
Hourly rate was never stated. On a call whose entire purpose was a quote, no price per mover per hour was given.
Nothing on what's included — no gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, or tools.
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no 'no hidden fees' pitch.
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.

Clock mechanics only surfaced because the customer asked — Brandon raised the 2.5 hour minimum himself ('is it the two and a half hour minimum?'). Clock-starts-on-site and the 15-minute increments were never explained, and no sense-check.
Never asked about packing services.
Never asked how many boxes — on a 1400 sqft two-bedroom being staged through storage.
Never asked about moving stressors or what the customer was worried about.
Zero Save Your Ass content. This was a storage-then-close move with a week between legs — the single best carload/consolidation setup on the board — and no prep speech was given.
Sparefoot referral missed. Customer said 'we kind of have a storage unit lined up' and Joel answered 'we don't do any onsite storing' with no referral offered.
Ecobox never mentioned despite an obvious box need.

Estimate pushback went unresolved. Brandon said 'Oh, wow. I think it took us like three hours' against Joel's 6.5-7.5 hour day-one number; Joel replied 'yes sir' and left a 2x discrepancy sitting there.
Never offered a three-mover crew option even after the customer said his prior move used three movers.
No estimate variables explained — stairs/elevator, walk distance, and the extra stop were measured but never tied to time or cost.
No booking attempt. Customer said 'let me think about that and I'll get back to you' and Joel closed with 'alright, thank you, bye-bye' — no availability offer, no ask.
'No deposit required' never mentioned.
No 'any other questions before I let you go?', no hours, no how-to-reach-us.
Customer's name never used once in 7.4 minutes.
Clarity problems — the hour estimate was garbled badly enough that Brandon misheard it as '67 hours' twice and Joel never cleanly restated it.
top_strength: The best moment was recalling the existing quote in specific detail without being asked to dig: 'we sent a quote over to you on August 10th, it was for a two bedroom apartment on the sixteenth floor being moved to a storage unit on the first floor.' That instantly told Brandon he was known, and it let Joel work forward instead of restarting intake. His walk-distance probing was also genuinely good and appropriately granular — truck to elevator, then elevator to apartment door — and he caught the changed storage address rather than quoting the stale one on file. Asking the customer to send photos of everything to be moved was the right accuracy instinct.
coaching_note: Joel, this was a quote call where you never gave a price. That is the fix: before the call ends, the customer must hear the rate and what it buys — 'Pricing is super simple: it's a flat hourly rate for a two-mover crew, and that already includes the truck, gas, taxes, insurance, all the blankets, shrink wrap and bands, and the tools for any disassembly and reassembly. No credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, nothing tacked on at the end.' Brandon had to pull the 2.5 hour minimum out of you himself, which means the clock block never happened either. Second priority: you quoted roughly thirteen hours across two days and Brandon told you his last move took three hours with three movers — you answered 'yes sir' and let a 2x gap stand. That is the moment to say 'that's a fair question, let me tell you what's driving it: sixteenth floor with an elevator, two long walks, and a three-story unload — and let me price you a three-mover crew too, because more movers usually means fewer hours, not a bigger bill.' Third: this was a storage move with a week in between, which is the single best Save Your Ass setup you will get — 'anything you can take in your own car, especially loose stuff in drawers, kids' toys, garden tools, photos off the walls, is time you're not paying us for.' And say his name. You never said 'Brandon' once, and he left the call unbooked with no ask from you.
phone_presence_notes: Polite filler ('cool', 'sounds good', 'yes sir') but no affirmations of substance, zero name use, and the customer's one clear emotional cue — 'Oh, wow. I think it took us like three hours' — went completely unacknowledged.
audio_review_reason: Presence scored 2, and the transcript has multiple garbled stretches ('you're more than walking us in photos', 'with the score footage there') plus a customer mishearing the estimate twice — worth verifying whether this is flat delivery or a transcription/audio quality issue.
